frequency_question: How often does a highly partisan, restrictive voting bill pass both chambers (or specifically the Senate, depending on control) within a roughly one-year window?
membership_rule: Includes major standalone federal bills targeting voter registration requirements or election integrity introduced since 1995; excludes omnibus budget or general appropriations riders.

cases.name: Help America Vote Act (bipartisan, different class)
PROVE IT Act / similar restrictive proposals
Freedom to Vote Act (opposite partisan intent)

provenance_note: claimed 0 hits but 1 of 4 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 4 major representative categories named; standalone restrictive bills passing a split or counter-aligned Senate in this window are historically extremely rare.
known_gaps: Minor committee-level variants not reaching floor votes.
skeleton: Identified partisan election integrity bills introduced in polarized Congresses since 1995.
validity_reason: Based on long-term legislative polarization trends spanning multiple congressional sessions.
